llms.body:
# HackMD

> HackMD is a real-time collaborative Markdown workspace and knowledge base for individuals, classrooms, and teams. Every public note has a permanent URL with a plain-markdown alternate, designed so that humans, search engines, and LLM agents can all read the same content.

This file follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention. For machine-readable API discovery see [`/.well-known/api-catalog`](https://hackmd.io/.well-known/api-catalog) (RFC 9727). For crawl boundaries see [`/robots.txt`](https://hackmd.io/robots.txt) (RFC 9309).

## Reading notes as plain markdown

To read any public HackMD note as raw Markdown — avoiding heavy HTML parsing — use either of these methods:

- **URL suffix**: append `.md` to any note URL (e.g. `https://hackmd.io/@<user>/<slug-or-id>.md`)
- **HTTP header**: send a `GET` request to the bare URL with `Accept: text/markdown`

The HTML view also advertises this via `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown" href="…">`.

A `.md?no-meta` variant returns the markdown without YAML frontmatter, which is the cleanest form for LLM context.

Private notes return `HTTP 403 Forbidden` for both formats; do not retry.

## Acting on a user's behalf

When creating, editing, or managing notes on behalf of a user, always use the official API, CLI, or MCP server — **do not automate the web UI**.

Preferred surfaces (most to least context-efficient for agents):

1. [HackMD CLI](https://github.com/hackmdio/hackmd-cli) — shell-based; good for scripting and on-demand help
2. [HackMD MCP](#hackmd-mcp-model-context-protocol) — remote server for chat-native clients (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, …)
3. [HackMD REST API v1](#programmatic-access-hackmd-api-v1) — direct HTTP integration

The CLI and REST API require a user-issued API token ([Settings → API](https://hackmd.io/settings#api), sign-in required). The MCP server uses OAuth instead — see [HackMD MCP](#hackmd-mcp-model-context-protocol) below.

## Discovering content

- [Sitemap index](https://hackmd.io/sitemap.xml) — partitioned into `home`, per-note shards, per-user shards, per-team shards, and a `fresh` shard for recently active public notes. Every entry has `<lastmod>`.
- A note is included in the sitemap when it is publicly published *and* has crossed an interaction threshold; it is removed automatically when taken down.
- [Community](https://hackmd.io/community) — browse and follow public notes from other HackMD users.

## Programmatic access (HackMD API v1)

- [Developers hub](https://hackmd.io/developers) — canonical entry for API and MCP documentation
- [API catalog](https://hackmd.io/.well-known/api-catalog) — RFC 9727 linkset; entry point for agents (REST + MCP)
- [HackMD REST API (OpenAPI)](https://api.hackmd.io/v1/docs/swagger.json) — OpenAPI 3.0 specification (raw JSON)
- [Swagger UI](https://api.hackmd.io/v1/docs/) — interactive documentation
- [HackMD CLI](https://github.com/hackmdio/hackmd-cli) — command-line interface
- [Developer Portal](https://hackmd.io/@docs/developer-portal)
- [Getting Started with the HackMD API](https://hackmd.io/@docs/Getting-Started-with-the-HackMD-API)
- [Authentication: Bearer token](https://hackmd.io/@docs/api-authorization)
- [How to issue an API token](https://hackmd.io/@docs/how-to-issue-an-api-token) — or open [Settings → API](https://hackmd.io/settings#api) directly
- [API usage policy & rate limits](https://hackmd.io/@docs/api-policy) — free tier: 2,000 calls/month, 100 calls per 5 minutes; monitor via `X-RateLimit-*` response headers
- [Attachments API](https://hackmd.io/@docs/attachments-api)
- [API changelog](https://hackmd.io/@docs/changelog)
- [Status page](https://status.hackmd.io/)

> **Moved paths:** API documentation formerly at `hackmd.io/@hackmd-api/*` now lives under `hackmd.io/@docs/*`. The old `@hackmd-api` URLs redirect with HTTP 301.

## HackMD MCP (Model Context Protocol)

HackMD hosts an official remote MCP server so AI assistants can read and write notes inside a conversation.

The MCP server authenticates with **OAuth 2.1**. The REST API and CLI continue to use personal API tokens; the two are independent.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Server URL** | `https://mcp.hackmd.io/` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 (authorization code + PKCE) |
| **Scope** | `mcp` |
| **Resource metadata** | [`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`](https://mcp.hackmd.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource) (RFC 9728) |
| **Authorization server** | `https://hackmd.io` — see [`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`](https://hackmd.io/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server) |

### Connecting

Most MCP clients need only the server URL; the client opens a browser window for you to approve access. No API token is required.

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "hackmd": { "url": "https://mcp.hackmd.io/" } } }
```

Unauthenticated requests — including `tools/list` — return **HTTP 401** with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="mcp"` challenge pointing at the resource metadata above. There is no public tool catalog.

- [HackMD MCP Server Setup](https://hackmd.io/@docs/hackmd-mcp-setup) — per-client configuration, full tool list, troubleshooting
- Alternate entry: [MCP setup (developer portal book)](https://hackmd.io/@docs/mcp-server-setup)

### Legacy: API token authentication

Clients that cannot complete an OAuth flow may still authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <API_TOKEN>`, typically via the `mcp-remote` bridge. This path is kept for compatibility only; prefer OAuth. See the setup guide for the exact configuration.

### Tools and resources

Tool names use **kebab-case** (e.g. `list-notes`, `get-note`, `create-note`, `search-notes`). Do not guess `snake_case` names.

Representative tools: `list-notes`, `get-note`, `create-note`, `update-note`, `delete-note`, `list-teams`, `get-team`, `search-notes`, `get-history`, `get-me`. Pass the optional `teamPath` parameter to `list-notes` or `create-note` for a team workspace. See the setup guide for the complete list and parameters.

MCP resources (URI scheme `hackmd://`): `hackmd://notes/{noteId}` (markdown), `hackmd://me` (JSON profile), `hackmd://teams/{teamPath}` (JSON team details).

## AI use policy

- AI **search & answer engines** (e.g. ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews) **may** crawl publicly published notes and cite them with attribution.
- AI **foundation-model training** is **not permitted**. See [`/robots.txt`](https://hackmd.io/robots.txt) for the per-vendor declarations (`GPTBot`, `Google-Extended`, `ClaudeBot`, `Applebot-Extended`, `CCBot`, `Meta-ExternalAgent`, `Bytespider`, etc. all `Disallow: /`).
- **User-initiated agents** acting on a logged-in user's behalf may use MCP OAuth or that user's API token under the API policy linked above.
- **Private notes** (HTTP 403 to anonymous requests) must not be accessed, transcribed, or retained.

## Product & company pages

- [About HackMD](https://hackmd.io/about)
- [Features](https://hackmd.io/features)
- [Pricing](https://hackmd.io/pricing)
- [Solutions](https://hackmd.io/solutions)
- [Enterprise](https://hackmd.io/enterprise)
- [Community](https://hackmd.io/community)
- [Blog](https://hackmd.io/blog)
- [Changelog](https://hackmd.io/changelog)
- [Release notes](https://hackmd.io/s/release-notes)
- [Terms of Service](https://hackmd.io/s/terms)
- [Privacy Policy](https://hackmd.io/s/privacy)

## Tutorials and example corpora

- [Tutorials (English)](https://hackmd.io/c/tutorials)
- [中文教學](https://hackmd.io/c/tutorials-tw)
- [YAML metadata reference](https://hackmd.io/yaml-metadata)

## Optional

- Each note also exposes Open Graph and Twitter card metadata (`og:url`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `twitter:*`) for link unfurling.
- The HTML view sets `<link rel="canonical">` to the bare URL `https://hackmd.io/@<user>/<slug>`. Always use this canonical form when citing.
- For agents that need the full API + MCP context in one fetch, start at [Developers hub](https://hackmd.io/developers) and follow links to the Developer Portal book and MCP setup guide.

Your team has ideas,

HackMD brings them together

Teams are shipping faster than ever
AI agents handle drafts, code generation, research, and documentation. But there's a disconnect that's slowing everything down: the place where your team thinks, plans, and refines their work isn't the same place your agents can access it.
What's missing is a shared layer
Your team and your agents should always be working from the same source of truth, a place where the team sets direction, agents contribute, and everything stays aligned as ideas move from rough draft to polished output ready to ship.
That's where HackMD comes in
It's not just a collaboration tool for your team, but the shared context layer that keeps your team and your agents in sync. Your team refines ideas in one place, agents pull from that same place, and when agents contribute something back, it lands right where the team can review, edit, and build on it together.

Millions build with HackMD's Markdown editor every day

Powering teams around the world, from next-generation startups to established institutions

Your team has ideas,

Teams are shipping faster than ever
AI agents handle drafts, code generation, research, and documentation. But there's a disconnect that's slowing everything down: the place where your team thinks, plans, and refines their work isn't the same place your agents can access it.
What's missing is a shared layer
Your team and your agents should always be working from the same source of truth, a place where the team sets direction, agents contribute, and everything stays aligned as ideas move from rough draft to polished output ready to ship.
That's where HackMD comes in
It's not just a collaboration tool for your team, but the shared context layer that keeps your team and your agents in sync. Your team refines ideas in one place, agents pull from that same place, and when agents contribute something back, it lands right where the team can review, edit, and build on it together.
